nodes.description: Persistence of the fetal linear i antigen on adult red cells with very low I expression. Serologically striking and clinically benign: it is a marker of the enzyme defect rather than a disease manifestation, and is recorded here because it is the trait that led to the gene.

evidence.reference_title: A novel IGnT allele responsible for the adult i phenotype.
evidence.snippet: The adult i phenotype has been characterized as the presence of a very low level of I antigen but a high quantity of I antigen on red blood cells (RBCs).

nodes.description: Early lens extraction with subsequent refractive correction and amblyopia management. The treatment is the same as for congenital cataract of any cause, is not directed at the glycosylation defect, and the enzyme deficiency itself is untreated.
Bilateral congenital cataract, of varying morphology across reported families.

evidence.reference_title: Case Report With Biallelic Variants in GCNT2 Implicates Exon 1B in Congenital Cataracts.
evidence.snippet: GCNT2-related cataracts is a disorder characterized by bilateral congenital cataracts (CC) of various types (with or without the adult i blood phenotype) and is caused by biallelic variants in GCNT2

nodes.description:
The I antigen is present on lens epithelium as well as on red cells, and loss of branching there is what produces the cataract. The isoform expression data put the lens-relevant transcripts and the erythroid transcript on different exon 1 variants, which is what makes the two consequences separable.
How the loss of a glycan branch actually causes lens opacification is not established. The published work demonstrates that GCNT2 is expressed in lens epithelium and that its loss co-segregates with cataract; it does not demonstrate the intervening step, whether that is altered membrane protein trafficking, osmotic change, or protein aggregation. This node therefore states the association and stops there rather than supplying a mechanism the literature does not.

evidence.reference_title: The molecular genetics of the human I locus and molecular background explain the partial association of the adult i phenotype with congenital cataracts.
evidence.snippet: enzyme function assays and expression patterns for the 3 IGnT transcripts in reticulocytes and lens-epithelium cells were analyzed

evidence.reference_title: The molecular genetics of the human I locus and molecular background explain the partial association of the adult i phenotype with congenital cataracts.
evidence.snippet: The results suggest a molecular genetic mechanism that may explain the partial association of the adult i phenotype with congenital cataracts and indicate that a defect in the I locus may lead directly to the development of congenital cataracts.

nodes.description: Biallelic GCNT2 variants abolish or greatly reduce I-branching beta-1,6-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase activity. Reported alleles include nonsense variants in shared exon 2 that truncate all three isoforms at once, frameshifts, and large Alu-mediated deletions removing whole exons. A missense allele in exon 1C has been shown by direct enzyme assay to reduce rather than abolish activity, which is the finer-grained version of the same lesion.

evidence.reference_title: The molecular genetics of the human I locus and molecular background explain the partial association of the adult i phenotype with congenital cataracts.
evidence.snippet: The human i and I antigens are characterized as linear and branched repeats of N-acetyllactosamine, respectively. Conversion of the i to the I structure requires I-branching beta-1,6-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase activity.

evidence.reference_title: A nonsense mutation in the glucosaminyl (N-acetyl) transferase 2 gene (GCNT2): association with autosomal recessive congenital cataracts.
evidence.snippet: revealed in these families a homozygous G-->A substitution in base 58 of exon-2, resulting in the formation of premature stop codons W328X, W326X, and W328X, of the GCNT2A, -B, and -C isoforms, respectively

evidence.reference_title: A novel IGnT allele responsible for the adult i phenotype.
evidence.snippet: The activity of the IGnT enzyme expressed from the mutant IGnTC*243A gene was significantly reduced when compared with that expressed from the wild-type IGnTC gene.

nodes.description: Without I-branching activity the erythrocyte surface keeps the fetal linear i structure into adult life instead of converting to branched I. This is the serologically detectable adult i blood group, and it is benign: it causes no haemolysis and no clinical consequence on its own. Its value here is as a marker of the enzymatic lesion, which is how the gene was found in the first place.

evidence.reference_title: Pleiotropic effect of a novel mutation in GCNT2 causing congenital cataract and a rare adult i blood group phenotype.
evidence.snippet: i antigens are predominant on fetal red blood cells, whereas adult human red blood cells fully express I antigens with a very low level of i antigens. The conversion of i to I occurs during the first 18 months after birth as a result of the expression of the I-branching enzyme

evidence.reference_title: An Alu repeat-mediated genomic GCNT2 deletion underlies congenital cataracts and adult i blood group.
evidence.snippet: we showed that cataract-affected individuals in both families have the adult i blood group, whereas unaffected individuals have blood group I as the vast majority of the population

nodes.description: Consequent on the cataract. Congenital cataract is among the leading causes of childhood blindness, which is what makes the timing of surgery the whole of the management question here.

evidence.reference_title: Case report of homozygous deletion involving the first coding exons of GCNT2 isoforms A and B and part of the upstream region of TFAP2A in congenital cataract.
evidence.snippet: Congenital cataracts affect 3-6 per 10,000 live births and represent one of the leading causes of blindness in children.
